blocks.title: What is this file?
blocks.what: This file runs a Pod with health checks. It comes from the core v1 API.
blocks.why: Probes work the same in a Pod and in a Deployment’s Pod template. A single Pod is easier to watch.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because it cannot tell what you want to create.
blocks.comment: What to create: a Pod, from the core v1 API

blocks.title: Give it a name
blocks.why: You use the name to watch its health and run commands inside it.
blocks.ifRemoved: Kubernetes rejects the file, because every object needs a name.
blocks.comment: A name to find the Pod
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: probe-demo

blocks.title: What should run?
blocks.what: One nginx container that serves a web page on port 80. This block makes the file ready.
blocks.why: Without probes, Kubernetes only knows whether the process is running, not whether it works.
blocks.ifRemoved: Without containers, Kubernetes rejects the Pod.
blocks.comment: The container to run and check
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: probe-demo
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: nginx:1.30.4
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80

blocks.title: Has it started?
blocks.what: The startup probe asks for the home page every 3 seconds, up to 10 times.
blocks.why: Slow apps get time to start. The other probes wait until this one passes.
blocks.ifRemoved: The other probes start at once and may restart a slow app too early.
blocks.comment: Wait up to 30 seconds for the app to start
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: probe-demo
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: nginx:1.30.4
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80
      startupProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /
          port: 80
        failureThreshold: 10
        periodSeconds: 3

blocks.title: Is it ready for traffic?
blocks.what: The readiness probe asks for the page every 5 seconds while the Pod runs.
blocks.why: While it fails, Services stop sending traffic to this Pod. Nothing is restarted.
blocks.ifRemoved: The Pod counts as ready as soon as it starts, even if the app cannot answer yet.
blocks.comment: Only send traffic while the page answers
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: probe-demo
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: nginx:1.30.4
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80
      startupProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /
          port: 80
        failureThreshold: 10
        periodSeconds: 3
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /
          port: 80
        periodSeconds: 5

blocks.title: Is it still working?
blocks.what: The liveness probe asks every 10 seconds. After 3 failures in a row, Kubernetes restarts the container.
blocks.why: A restart fixes apps that are stuck but still running.
blocks.ifRemoved: A stuck container keeps running and never recovers.
blocks.comment: Restart the container if the page stops answering
blocks.yaml:
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: probe-demo
spec:
  containers:
    - name: web
      image: nginx:1.30.4
      ports:
        - containerPort: 80
      startupProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /
          port: 80
        failureThreshold: 10
        periodSeconds: 3
      readinessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /
          port: 80
        periodSeconds: 5
      livenessProbe:
        httpGet:
          path: /
          port: 80
        periodSeconds: 10
        failureThreshold: 3

notes.apiVersion: The API group and version that define this kind. Pods are in the core v1 API.
notes.kind: The type of object to create. A Pod runs one or more containers together.
notes.metadata: Details that identify the object, such as its name.
notes.metadata.name: The Pod’s name. kubectl get and kubectl exec use it.
notes.spec: The desired state: what you want Kubernetes to run.
notes.spec.containers: The containers in this Pod. Each list item starts with a dash.
notes.spec.containers[].name: The container’s name. Probe messages in events name it.
notes.spec.containers[].image: The nginx web server, pinned to a version.
notes.spec.containers[].ports: Ports the container listens on. This list is mostly informational.
notes.spec.containers[].ports[].containerPort: nginx listens on port 80 inside the container.
notes.spec.containers[].startupProbe: Checks whether the app has started. The other probes wait until it passes.
notes.spec.containers[].startupProbe.httpGet: Check by asking for a web page. Any status from 200 to 399 passes.
notes.spec.containers[].startupProbe.httpGet.p: The page to ask for: /, nginx’s home page.
The port to ask on. It must be where the app listens: 80.
notes.spec.containers[].startupProbe.periodSec: How many seconds to wait between checks.
notes.spec.containers[].startupProbe.failureTh: Allow 10 failed checks, about 30 seconds, before restarting the container.
notes.spec.containers[].readinessProbe: Checks whether the app can take traffic. Failing removes the Pod from Services.
notes.spec.containers[].readinessProbe.httpGet: Check by asking for a web page. Any status from 200 to 399 passes.
The page to ask for: /, nginx’s home page.
The port to ask on. It must be where the app listens: 80.
notes.spec.containers[].readinessProbe.periodS: How many seconds to wait between checks.
notes.spec.containers[].livenessProbe: Checks whether the app still works. Failing too often restarts the container.
notes.spec.containers[].livenessProbe.httpGet: Check by asking for a web page. Any status from 200 to 399 passes.
The page to ask for: /, nginx’s home page.
The port to ask on. It must be where the app listens: 80.
notes.spec.containers[].livenessProbe.periodSe: How many seconds to wait between checks.
notes.spec.containers[].livenessProbe.failureT: Restart after 3 failed checks in a row, about 30 seconds.

tryIt.result: READY shows 1/1 once the startup and readiness probes pass.
Prints nothing. Deleting the home page makes nginx answer / with 403 Forbidden, so the probes start failing.
Within about 15 seconds, READY drops to 0/1. Services stop sending traffic, but nothing restarts yet.
Events show Liveness probe failed with status code 403, then the container failed liveness probe and will be restarted.

expect: Liveness probe failed: HTTP probe failed with statuscode: 403
failed liveness probe, will be restarted

tryIt.result: RESTARTS shows 1 and READY is back to 1/1. The new container has a fresh home page.

questions.question: Which probe decides whether the container is restarted?
questions.explain: A failing liveness probe restarts the container. A failing startup probe does too, but only while starting.

questions.question: The readiness probe fails, but the liveness probe passes. What happens?
answers: The Pod keeps running but gets no Service traffic
questions.explain: Readiness only controls traffic. The Pod waits until the probe passes again.

questions.question: How long can nginx take to start before the startup probe gives up?
questions.explain: Ten checks, 3 seconds apart, give the app about 30 seconds to start.

fix.expect: Readiness probe failed: Get "http://[\d.]+:8080/": dial tcp [\d.]+:8080: connect: connection refused
fix.message: Readiness probe failed: Get "http://<Pod IP>:8080/": dial tcp <Pod IP>:8080: connect: connection refused
fix.explain: nginx listens on port 80, so nothing answers on 8080. The Pod never becomes ready, so it never gets traffic.
fix.fix: Point the probe at the port the app listens on: port: 80.
